items.title: Chazz Frichtel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 13, 2016
items.q: Chick — we got together in L.A. one time. He took a trip to L.A. and it was really, really great to see him.

ctx.x: You had Esposito and Montalbano and Robilatto. This area had so many great musicians of Italian descent.

Oh man, I can’t tell you how much Dick Robilatto, what kind of influence he had on my life. And I was lucky enough that I got him on the phone not too long before he passed away. I’m not even sure he knew for certain who he was talking to. But he said, “Yeah I had a student Charlie who went out to L.A. I think he’s doing okay out there.” And it was just so touching. He was my high school band director. He was such a wonderful guy. But that’s, you know I have said time and time again I feel such a debt to the…

I’ve told Rick and Carmen that too. Because when I first moved up here I managed to get a gig with the both of them and Dolores Mancuso at the Beeches. And I just sat on my stool with my sax and I watched and listened to what they did. And I thought I knew a lot because I had gone to music school. But I didn’t know anything about playing gigs and filling what people’s expectations would be, or beyond. It was really an education for me.
